question: How do motorist and cyclist deaths compare year by year in NYC, 2013 to 2025?

options.metric: Annual number of motorist deaths (number_of_motorist_killed) and cyclist deaths (number_of_cyclist_killed) recorded in NYC crashes, compared as separate series.
options.denominator: None; absolute death counts summed from the two road-user-specific killed fields.
options.grouping: Calendar year, with two series: motorist deaths and cyclist deaths.
options.reason: Absolute yearly counts provide the most direct year-by-year comparison of the two requested types of deaths.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths every year; in 2025 the counts were 81 versus 23, and the period highs were 139 motorist deaths in 2020 and 31 cyclist deaths in 2019 and 2023.
options.interpretation: Summing number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed by calendar year answers the requested absolute-count comparison: motorist deaths exceed cyclist deaths every year, motorist totals peak in 2020, and cyclist totals peak in 2019 and 2023. Paired bars are a defensible direct comparison of the two annual fatality series, but this framing does not measure per-person or per-trip risk or explain causes. The check file records 2,132,218 in-range crash rows, complete January 1–December 31 coverage in each of 13 years, and no missing values in either killed field, so all in-range rows are kept with no missing-outcome exclusions. These are recorded totals in police-reported NYC crashes; the actual parquet fields are number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed.

options.metric: Annual share of the combined motorist-and-cyclist deaths (number_of_motorist_killed plus number_of_cyclist_killed) accounted for by motorist deaths and cyclist deaths.
options.denominator: For each year, motorist deaths plus cyclist deaths; other road-user deaths are outside this denominator.
options.grouping: Calendar year and road-user category (motorist or cyclist); each annual category count is divided by the year's combined motorist and cyclist deaths.
options.reason: Annual shares show how the balance between the two requested death categories changes independently of the combined yearly total.
options.answer: Cyclists accounted for 9.1%–27.4% of annual motorist-plus-cyclist deaths, peaking at 27.4% in 2019, while motorists accounted for the remainder.
options.interpretation: For each calendar year, the motorist share is summed motorist deaths divided by summed motorist plus cyclist deaths, and the cyclist share is defined analogously; this answers how the relative mix compares, with cyclist share highest at 27.4% in 2019 and motorist share highest at 90.9% in 2013. A 100% stacked annual chart is defensible for this composition question, but it leaves absolute death counts, other road-user deaths, and population exposure or risk unanswered. The check file records 2,132,218 in-range crash rows, complete January 1–December 31 coverage in all 13 years, and zero missing values in either killed field, so all rows are retained without missing-outcome handling. The denominator intentionally contains only the two specified death categories, not all fatalities; the parquet fields are number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed.

answer:
- Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths every year; in 2025 the counts were 81 versus 23, with period highs of 139 motorist deaths in 2020 and 31 cyclist deaths in both 2019 and 2023.
- Cyclists accounted for 9.1%–27.4% of annual motorist-plus-cyclist deaths, peaking at 27.4% in 2019; motorists made up the remainder.
